thread:
Samir K: Quick heads-up — RFC follow-up: we need a rollout plan for clients that will start sending Content-Type: application/redwood.v2+json. Two approaches: CDN edge normalizer vs runtime shim. Thoughts?
Ava L: +1. Edge is tempting for latency but splitting normalization across infra/runtime worries me. Need clear ownership.
Diego: Edge fn is doable (Fastly/CF worker). Latency impact is tiny (<2ms). Biggest ops risk is coupling deploys to CDN config + slower rollback if misbehaves. Feature-flagging at CDN layer exists but is clunkier.
Priya: Runtime shim (ingress proxy) is trivial: inspect Content-Type, normalize to application/json, set X-RI-Normalizer=runtime then pass downstream. Centralized observability and easier for Private deployments. Perf hit small (~0.2-0.5ms) but consistent.
Samir K: Other considerations: signed requests and mutual-TLS for Private — edge won't see those for on-prem. Also TLS termination differences.
Ava L: Security point — if edge rewrites headers before WAF runs we might miss dangerous payload shapes. If we go edge-first, ensure WAF is applied after normalization or duplicate checks.
Jon: Telemetry: we should emit metric normalizer.path {value: edge|runtime|none} and attach X-RI-Normalizer header so we can slice by who normalized. Also log the original Content-Type for debugging.
infra-bot: Deploy note: edge-normalizer prototype deployed to prod-edge-alpha (canary 1%) at 1719456500. Observability pipeline receiving logs.
Diego: Important: Hosted can use edge normalizer to reduce p99, but Private customers (VPC/on-prem) won't benefit. If we only did edge, Private would break unless they update clients — not acceptable.
Priya: Proposal: hybrid rollout. (A) Implement lightweight runtime shim in ingress that is backward-compatible and idempotent. (B) Deploy edge normalizer for Hosted only to reduce latency. Runtime shim acts as fallback and as single compatibility contract for Private.
Samir K: Nice. Fallback semantics: edge sets X-RI-Normalizer=edge and short-circuits if downstream already normalized. Runtime checks X-RI-Normalizer and is no-op when present.
Ava L: Runbook: include rollback steps for edge fn, feature-flag toggles, metric thresholds (error rate >0.5% or p99 increase >10%), and who to page. I'll draft.
Diego: I'll prototype edge worker and include a fast revert toggle. PR will include short perf run and e2e against gateway.
Priya: I'll add middleware to ingress (k8s-ingress/proxy) + unit tests and a perf benchmark harness. Also add integration test that simulates Private env.
Samir K: Action items: Diego -> edge prototype + flag by EOW; Priya -> runtime middleware + tests; Ava -> rollout doc and metrics; infra -> coordinate canaries and WAF ordering.
Ava L: I'll add a telemetry schema: metric name redwood.normalizer.path, tag content_type_original, tag client_version. Also add a short log line: "normalized from %s by %s".
Jon: Suggest we also add a warning header for clients: X-RI-Compat-Warn: will deprecate redwood.v1 by <date>. Helps client library maintainers.
Priya: Good call. We'll ensure runtime inserts the warning when it normalizes v1 -> v2 mapping.
Samir K: Ok. We'll discuss the specific rollout percentages and SLA targets in tomorrow's arch sync. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
